Documentation → FortiWeb: Policies & Protection → Template library

Template library

A versioned library of desired-state templates (web protection profiles, system profiles, server policies, structures and captured configuration objects) with an approval workflow and a dry-run-first, canary-first apply.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsoperations.view operations.template_save operations.template_apply operations.apply operations.template_approve
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Administrator → Template Library; FortiWeb ADOM → Operations → Template Library (users without users.manage) (URL /templates)

What is it?#

The Template Library stores reusable desired-state configuration as named, versioned JSON templates. A template is authored or captured once, reviewed by an administrator, and then pushed to one or many devices on demand. Editing never overwrites: saving produces a new version and the previous one stays.

What does it do?#

  • Lists templates of four built-in kinds — Web Protection Profile, Server Policy, System Profile, Structure — plus configuration templates captured from Configuration sections (kind config:<section>).
  • Shows Kind, Name, Version, Firmware, Status (pending / approved / rejected), Note, Author and Created for each template.
  • Records the firmware build each template body was written for and the REST API version, checks the body against that build when it is saved and against every target's build when it is applied. See Firmware build and compatibility.
  • Filters by kind (All and one button per built-in kind), by status (Pending, Approved) and by free text (Search templates…).
  • Creates, views, edits (as a new version), clones and deletes templates.
  • Runs an approval workflow: approve, reject with a reason, revoke approval, and an Approval history timeline per template.
  • Applies a template to devices with a mandatory Dry-run preview, then a live push that runs canary-first as a background job.
  • Shows, for every binding in the template dialog, a Compliance column — met, deviates or unmeasured, with the reason in the tooltip — computed on this node from the cached device objects, without contacting the device. The same comparison raises the Intent deviation finding of the alert engine.
  • Is readable and, with the explicit capabilities template_draft and template_apply, writable through the REST API: templates, versions, bindings and baselines, with an apply that follows the console's own dry-run and canary path.

NAF block: Intent. Templates, bindings and baselines are SATOM's desired state — what the Network Automation Forum's framework calls Intent. (The "Source of Truth" is the actual state, NAF's Observability.) See Where SATOM sits in the NAF Framework.

Templates also arrive from other pages:

Source Button Kind created
Web Protection Profile page Save as template (needs admin approval) Web Protection Profile
Configuration sections / WAF areas, inline editor Save as template config:<section>
Configuration sections, library card New template config:<section>
Factory catalog entry Save as template Web Protection Profile (provenance factory)

Every new template or new version lands pending.

Requirements#

  • At least one appliance registered (for applying).
  • Templates are scoped to the active ADOM: the FortiADC ADOM sees only FortiADC templates, the FortiWeb ADOM everything else, the Global ADOM all of them.

Permissions#

Action Required
Open the library, view a template, view approval history operations.view
New Template, Edit, Clone, Delete, Save as template operations.template_save
Apply to one device (any status) operations.template_apply
Apply to several devices (fleet rollout) operations.template_apply and operations.apply, and the template must be approved
Approve, Reject, Revoke approval operations.template_approve (Administrator only)
Check against fleet builds (View dialog) operations.view
Revalidate for fleet builds (View dialog), override a blocked apply with a reason operations.template_approve
Adapt to firmware (View dialog) operations.template_save
FortiWeb Sections button users.manage

🔑Permission — What users without permission see

Administrators (users.manage) find Template Library in the Administrator group. Every other user with operations.view finds it in the Operations group. On the page, the approve/reject/revoke, apply and edit/clone/delete buttons are shown only to users holding the matching permission. New Template is shown to everyone; saving without operations.template_save returns the 403 page.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.12.0: templates record the firmware build and REST API version they were written for (the new Firmware column), are checked against that build at save and against each target's build at apply, approval records the builds a template was validated for (Revalidate for fleet builds extends it), and Adapt to firmware saves a version rewritten for another build. Templates can also be saved from the Factory catalog.

⚠️Warning — Upgrading to 2.12.0

Templates saved before 2.12.0 show no firmware. Already-approved templates have no validated builds, so their fleet rollouts and baseline applies are refused until an approver clicks Revalidate for fleet builds in the View dialog, once per template. Single-device applies are only checked field by field.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: operators without users.manage now find the Template Library under Operations, the canary of an apply is the first selected device in the list, and approving a Web Protection Profile template rolls it out to FortiWeb devices only.

How to use#

Create a template#

  1. Click New Template.
  2. Choose Kind, enter Name, choose Written for firmware (the build the body was written for), and enter an optional Note, the Body (JSON) and optional Exceptions (JSON).
  3. Click Save Template. The flash reads Template "<name>" saved (vN).

⚠️Warning — Keep secrets out of the body

The body is stored as entered and pushed as is. The apply dialog has no field for secrets, so do not rely on entering passwords or keys at apply time.

Edit, clone or delete#

  • Edit (saves a new version) opens Edit Template; the kind is fixed. Save New Version stores vN+1 and leaves the earlier version unchanged. The new version is pending again.
  • Clone copies body and exceptions to <name> (copy).
  • Delete asks Delete template '<name>' (vN)? This cannot be undone. Locked templates (lock icon) cannot be deleted.

Review a template (administrators)#

  1. Click Pending to list templates awaiting review.
  2. Click View to read the body and exceptions.
  3. Click Approve (make fleet-deployable), or Reject and fill in Reason (shown to the author) → Reject template.
  4. To withdraw an approval, click Revoke approval (back to pending) and confirm.
  5. Approval history shows every approve, reject and revoke with reviewer, time and reason.

Approving also records the builds the template was validated for: its own build plus every build its product runs among the devices visible to you. The flash reads Approved "<name>" vN — validated for <builds>. When the body does not fit one of those builds, a second message reads "<name>" vN does not fit <builds>: applying it there is refused until it is adapted (or an approver overrides with a reason).

❗Important — Approving a Web Protection Profile template deploys it

Approving a template of kind Web Protection Profile immediately starts a rollout of that template to every FortiWeb visible to you in the current ADOM (FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator devices are skipped), as a background job (Deploying "<name>" vN to ALL N device(s) — progress in the job dock.). A profile managed by an approved template becomes read-only on the device pages; change it here instead.

Apply a template#

  1. Click Apply to devices on the template row.
  2. Select one or more Target devices (Ctrl/Cmd for several). The canary is the selected device that comes first in the list. Only devices visible to you are accepted.
  3. Click Dry-run preview. For each device you see ok or error and the list of requests (action METHOD path), and the Firmware compatibility card with a verdict per device. Nothing is sent.
  4. If the card says blocked, a user with operations.template_approve can type an Override reason (required to proceed; audited). Without that permission the card reads Applying is refused. Adapt the template to the target build, or ask an approver (Approve templates permission) to override with a reason. and the confirm button stays disabled.
  5. Click Confirm live apply. The flash reads Rollout of "<name>" vN started for N device(s) — progress appears in the job dock (bottom right).

The rollout writes to the canary first and continues with the other selected devices, in list order, only if the canary succeeds. On each device it stops at the first failed write. The job can be stopped from the job dock; it halts between items and devices.

Firmware build and compatibility#

FortiWeb answers a write that carries a field its build does not know with HTTP 200 and discards the field. A template written on one build can therefore be applied to another, report success and land incomplete. Each template now records the build it belongs to, and SATOM checks it.

Stamp. The Firmware column shows FW <build>, or no firmware for a template saved before builds were recorded. Hover the badge to see the provenance (captured, authored, adapted or factory), the source appliance and the API version.

  • Save as template on a Web Protection Profile or a configuration object records the appliance's running build (provenance captured).
  • New Template, the section New template form and System Provisioning ask for Written for firmware. Only builds SATOM knows are offered (API library, declared firmware, builds running in the fleet). A new version keeps its predecessor's build unless you pick another. When SATOM knows no build at all, the template is saved without one.
  • Factory catalog templates carry the catalog entry's build and API version (provenance factory).

Check at save. The body is compared against its own build through the API library. The Firmware column shows fits its build or does not fit its build next to the stamp.

Check at apply. Every apply path (this page, the section page, System Provisioning, baselines and the automatic rollout when a Web Protection Profile template is approved) shows a verdict per device for the device's running build:

Finding Effect
Every checked field is served by the build passes
A field the build would discard blocks
A field the build renamed blocks — adapt the template
An endpoint the build does not serve blocks
No evidence for the build, or the device reports no firmware warning, never a pass
Fleet rollout to a build the approval does not cover blocks — revalidate

Endpoints outside the API sweep are listed under Not checked (outside the API sweep):. A blocked apply proceeds only with an override reason from a holder of operations.template_approve; the override, its reason and what it overrode are written to the audit log.

Approval is for builds. The View dialog's Firmware & API compatibility card shows Checked against its own build when saved and Validated builds (approval). A fleet rollout (several devices, a baseline, a System Provisioning push) to a build outside the validated set is refused until an approver clicks Revalidate for fleet builds. A new version starts with no validations. Check against fleet builds runs the same check without recording anything.

Adapt to firmware. In the View dialog:

  1. Pick the target build under Adapt to firmware (— target build —).
  2. Click Preview. SATOM lists the renames it would carry to the new field name and the fields it would remove because the build does not serve them.
  3. Click Save adapted version. A new pending version is saved, stamped with the target build (provenance adapted), with every change listed in its note. The original version is unchanged.

A body whose object the target build does not serve at all cannot be adapted.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Kind Web Protection Profile, Server Policy, System Profile or Structure. Fixed after creation. Yes Web Protection Profile
Name Template name. Saving an existing kind + name creates the next version. Yes baseline-wpp
Written for firmware The build the body was written for, from the builds SATOM knows. Required while SATOM knows at least one build; a new version keeps its predecessor's build unless changed. Yes (see description) 7.6.8
Note Free description, shown in the list (long notes collapse behind see more). No Strict profile for shops
Body (JSON) The desired state. Must be a JSON object. Yes {"subobjects": [...]}
Exceptions (JSON) Optional exception rules carried with the template; a JSON object or array. No []

Example#

🧪Example — Promote a profile from one device to the fleet

  1. On fweb-01, open the Web Protection Profile page and use Save as template (needs admin approval) on wpp-shop → name wpp-shop-baseline.
  2. An administrator opens Template Library → Pending, views it and clicks Approve. Because it is a Web Protection Profile template, the rollout to all visible FortiWeb devices starts at once.
  3. For a config:system template instead, the operator clicks Apply to devices, selects fweb-02 and fweb-03, runs Dry-run preview, then Confirm live apply.

Result#

  • Audit entries: template.create, template.edit, template.clone, template.delete, template.approve, template.reject, template.unapprove, template.apply.preview, template.apply.start, and template.apply when the job finishes (template.approve.autodeploy for an approved Web Protection Profile).
  • Firmware checks write template.validate (Revalidate), template.adapt, template.compat.override (an override, with its reason), template.apply.refused and template.approve.autodeploy.held.
  • Approve, reject and revoke are kept in the template's approval history.
  • An apply runs as a job; see Jobs. The job ends as success, Aborted — canary device failed, Completed with failures, or stopped.
  • Approved templates appear in FortiWeb Sections and can be used in System Provisioning.

Troubleshooting#

"Template must be APPROVED before a multi-device (fleet) rollout."#

Possible causes - More than one target device is selected and the template is pending or rejected.

Solution 1. Apply to a single device to test it, or have an administrator approve it.

"Fleet rollout requires the Run operations permission."#

Possible causes - More than one target device is selected and you lack operations.apply.

Solution 1. Select one device, or ask for operations.apply.

"Refused by the firmware compatibility check: …"#

Possible causes - A target build would discard or has renamed fields of the body, or does not serve one of its endpoints. - A fleet rollout targets a build the approval does not cover (the approval does not cover build … — revalidate the template for it).

Solution 1. For a build outside the approval, an approver opens View and clicks Revalidate for fleet builds. 2. For discarded or renamed fields, use Adapt to firmware for that build and have the new version approved. 3. If writing the body is known to be safe, an approver applies it with an Override reason.

Verification — the dry-run preview shows no blocking finding.

"Fleet deploy of … HELD by the firmware check: …"#

Possible causes — The automatic rollout of an approved Web Protection Profile template found a blocking verdict on at least one FortiWeb. The approval itself is kept; nothing was deployed.

Solution — Adapt the template, or apply it from Apply to devices with an override reason.

"Only an approved template is validated for builds; approve it first."#

Revalidate for fleet builds works on approved templates only. Approve the template first.

"Firmware … is not a build SATOM knows for … — pick one from the list"#

Choose a build from Written for firmware; free-text builds are refused. Choose the firmware build this template is written for means none was chosen.

"nothing to adapt: every checked field of this template is served by …"#

The template already fits the target build; no new version is needed.

"… does not serve … — adapting fields cannot fix a missing object"#

The target build does not serve an endpoint the body writes, so no field rewrite can make it fit. Write a template for that build instead.

"Select at least one target device."#

Select one or more devices in Target devices before the preview.

"Unknown appliance."#

Possible causes - The request names a device you cannot see (another ADOM, or a device in maintenance mode without appliances.view_maintenance).

Solution 1. Reload the page and pick the devices from Target devices.

"Could not save template: Body is not valid JSON: …"#

Fix the JSON. Related messages: Template body must be a JSON object, Exceptions is not valid JSON: …, Template exceptions must be a JSON object or array, Template name is required.

"Template not found or locked."#

The template was already deleted or is locked; locked templates cannot be deleted.

The preview shows "error" for a device#

Possible causes - The body names endpoints or values that device cannot accept.

Solution 1. Read the error next to the failing request, fix the body (Edit → new version) and preview again.

Advanced#

Advanced Apply mechanics

The body is flattened into push items: a node's subobjects are emitted before the node itself, so referenced objects are created before the objects that use them. The preview builds the requests without contacting any device. The confirmed apply runs in a background job so that a large rollout is not cut off by an HTTP timeout; the job writes the completion audit entry.

Advanced Versions and status

Each version is a separate row with its own status. Editing an approved template creates a pending version; the approved version stays approved until revoked. A Web Protection Profile is treated as template-managed when its name matches any approved Web Protection Profile template.
